content: Primula elatior, commonly known as the oxlip or True oxlip, is a flowering plant belonging to the genus Primula. It is typically found in damp woodlands and meadows across Europe, extending as far north as southern Sweden. Within the British Isles, its distribution is limited to the eastern regions, predominantly in East Anglia. This plant is a low-growing, herbaceous perennial characterized by a basal rosette of leaves measuring between 5 to 15 cm in length and 2 to 6 cm in width. The flowers, which are a deep yellow color, bloom during the spring months of April and May. These flowers are arranged in clusters of 10 to 30 on a single stem that grows to a height of 10 to 30 cm. Each individual flower measures approximately 9 to 15 mm in diameter. Primula elatior can sometimes be mistaken for its closely related species, Primula veris, commonly known as cowslip. While both species share a similar overall appearance, the oxlip is distinguishable by its larger, pale yellow flowers that resemble those of a primrose. Additionally, the corolla tube of the oxlip lacks the folds that are characteristic of the cowslip.
